name: Early Dynastic & Old Kingdom Egypt
summary: Unified Upper and Lower Egypt around 3150 BCE. During the Old Kingdom (2686–2181 BCE), pharaohs marshaled national Nile flood-season labor to construct the Step Pyramid of Djoser and the Great Pyramids and Sphinx of Giza.
keyFacts: Great Pyramid of Giza (tallest human-made structure for 3,800 years)
Hieroglyphic writing, papyrus scrolls, and the 365-day solar calendar
Pyramid Texts—oldest religious corpus in the world

name: Egyptian Middle Kingdom
summary: Following the 4.2 kiloyear drought and First Intermediate Period, Mentuhotep II reunified Egypt, ushering in the golden age of classical Egyptian literature (Tale of Sinuhe), Faiyum land reclamation, and Red Sea expeditions to Punt.
keyFacts: Classical Middle Egyptian literature & mathematical papyri (Rhind & Moscow Papyri)
Canal of the Pharaohs linking the Nile to the Red Sea

name: Egyptian New Kingdom
summary: After expelling the Hyksos, New Kingdom pharaohs forged an empire from Nubia to the Euphrates, building Karnak, Luxor, the Valley of the Kings, and Abu Simbel, and surviving the Late Bronze Age Collapse.
keyFacts: Temple complexes of Karnak, Luxor, Deir el-Bahari, and Abu Simbel
Valley of the Kings royal tombs (including Tutankhamun’s intact tomb)
Amarna diplomatic archive & Kadesh Peace Treaty (1259 BCE)
